definitions.explanation: The time just before death; one's last moments of life.

examples.japanese: {臨終|りんじゅう}に{立|た}ち{会|あ}う。
{祖父|そふ}の{臨終|りんじゅう}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}わなかった。
examples.english: I didn't make it in time for my grandfather's final moments.

examples.japanese: {臨終|りんじゅう}の{際|さい}に{家族|かぞく}に{囲|かこ}まれていた。
examples.english: He was surrounded by family at the time of his passing.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}が{臨終|りんじゅう}を{告|つ}げると、{病室|びょうしつ}は{静|しず}まり{返|かえ}った。
examples.english: When the doctor announced the passing, the hospital room fell completely silent.

notes:
{臨|りん} (to face, to be present at) + {終|じゅう} (end). A solemn word describing the moment of approaching death. Originally a Buddhist term referring to the final moments before entering the next life.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {臨終|りんじゅう}に{立|た}ち{会|あ}う: be present at someone's deathbed
- {臨終|りんじゅう}を{迎|むか}える: face one's final moments
- {臨終|りんじゅう}を{告|つ}げる: announce someone's passing
- {臨終|りんじゅう}の{言葉|ことば}: last words
- {臨終|りんじゅう}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}う: make it in time for someone's final moments

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最期|さいご}: one's final moments, death — more literary and emotional
- {死|し}に{際|ぎわ}: the verge of death — emphasizes the boundary between life and death
- {往生|おうじょう}: passing away (Buddhist) — implies a peaceful death and rebirth in paradise

USAGE:
A formal and respectful word. Commonly heard in hospital settings when a doctor informs family members of a patient's passing. The phrase {臨終|りんじゅう}に{立|た}ち{会|あ}う (to be present at someone's deathbed) is considered important in Japanese culture.
